title: Quantum Dynamics of Observation Phase in the Physical–Observation Dual-Axis Structure
content: A quantum phase reference is part of the state from which an observation record emerges. Within the physical-observation dual-axis structure, we describe such a reference by a compact quantum coordinate coupled to a finite-dimensional physical system. A covariant rotor action gives the joint evolution and expresses the readout's phase acceleration through ordered correlations and a covariant force. In a qubit model whose dynamics preserve two adjacent observation momenta, the first harmonic depends on four complex correlations. For fixed nondegenerate parameters, its full complex history requires eight real state variables. For phase increments alone, a common amplitude and phase factor can be removed, leaving three complex correlation ratios. We prove that these six real variables are locally minimal at generic states for every fixed nondegenerate parameter choice. Six suitably timed phase estimates and an initial reference recover the ratios by solving real linear equations; an error bound relates uncertainty in those estimates to the subsequent phase prediction. The role of the retained correlations is illustrated by preparations with equal marginals and equal initial phase, rate, and acceleration, but different future phases. We also describe how the state continues through a zero of the first harmonic and how finite integration windows affect the available information. The resulting theory connects a joint quantum action to phase prediction from finite records, subject to independent physical characterization of the phase inertia and coupling.
